issue.title: Restore a green CI signal on sase master
issue.description: CI on sase master passes reliably: the sase_core_rs import defect can no longer poison a pytest-xdist worker, and the two racy ACE TUI tests assert against real synchronization points instead of wall-clock luck.

issue.title: Keep the core extension parent and submodule in sync across sys.modules patches
issue.description: modguard: give the six test modules that swap or evict sys.modules['sase_core_rs'] a shared helper that moves the compiled submodule with its parent package, and pin the re-import invariant with a regression test.

issue.title: Anchor the ACE title-refinement tests to the mount-loads sync point
issue.description: apptitle: replace the single pilot.pause() in the two on-mount title tests with a wait on _mount_state_loads_done, the barrier the title write actually sits behind.

issue.title: Make the rapid-navigation detail test drive the debouncer deterministically
issue.description: detailrace: stop assuming two keypresses land inside the 150 ms debounce window; control the timer the way the existing debouncer tests do and assert on the coalesced result.

issue.title: Harden the generated sase_core_rs package init upstream
issue.description: coreinit: fix the maturin star-import template in the sase-core repo so the package init binds the extension module explicitly instead of relying on an importlib side effect.

issue.title: Confirm the restored signal end to end
issue.description: verify: run the exhaustive local gate, re-run the failing legs under adverse conditions, and confirm a full CI run is green.

payload.entry: Replaced the single pilot.pause() in both on-mount title tests with a deadline-bounded poll on app._mount_state_loads_done (module-level _wait_for_mount_state_loads helper, following the ace_page.py:168/bench_tui_jk.py idiom). Fixed the sibling test too, as required. Verified: both tests pass (just install + pytest tests/ace/tui/test_app_title.py -v, 15/15 passed); confirmed the wait genuinely blocks by monkeypatching _run_mount_state_loads with a 0.5s artificial delay and observing the test still correctly asserts the resolved title; just check (fmt, lint, mypy, symvision, scoped tests) is green with only test_app_title.py modified.

Replaced the single pilot.pause() in both on-mount title tests with a deadline-bounded poll on app._mount_state_loads_done via a module-level _wait_for_mount_state_loads helper (matching ace_page.py:168 idiom); fixed the sibling resolver-returns-None test too. Verified: pytest tests/ace/tui/test_app_title.py -v (15/15 passed), an adversarial slow-loader check confirming the wait genuinely blocks, and a clean just check run.

PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: sase-core wheel-smoke CI job (crates/sase_core_py, .github/workflows/ci.yml) only checks a plain `import sase_core_rs`; it never exercises the del-sys.modules re-import path that caused this defect. Add a re-import smoke check (del sys.modules["sase_core_rs"]; importlib.import_module) to the wheel-smoke and release-plz smoke steps so a regression is caught before publish.

Fixed the root cause in sase-core: crates/sase_core_py now ships an explicit python/sase_core_rs/__init__.py (via python-source = "python" in pyproject.toml) that binds the compiled submodule by name instead of relying on importlib's post-import setattr side effect. Verified by building the wheel with maturin (release build, tag v0.18.4 source), installing into a fresh Python 3.12 venv, and reproducing the exact plan repro: del sys.modules['sase_core_rs'] then re-import now succeeds (previously NameError). Cross-checked that the currently-published wheel (installed in this sase workspace's .venv) still reproduces the original NameError under the same steps, confirming this is a real, fixed defect. __doc__/__all__ re-exports kept byte-compatible; cargo fmt --check passes (no Rust source touched). Opened https://github.com/sase-org/sase-core/pull/89 for review/merge to follow the repo's normal release-plz path; did not merge or publish myself since that triggers automated PyPI publish. Filed a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note on this bead for adding a re-import regression check to sase-core's wheel-smoke CI.

Rewrote test_rapid_navigation_loads_only_the_final_detail to intercept AceApp.set_timer instead of racing the 150ms debounce window: after two rapid j presses, calls==[] proves no timer fired yet (row-1 never loaded), then firing the captured callback manually yields calls==[rows[2].id]. Verified: pytest on the file passes (8/8), just check passes (all lint gates + scoped tests green).
Rewrote test_rapid_navigation_loads_only_the_final_detail to intercept AceApp.set_timer instead of racing the 150ms debounce window; verified pytest 8/8 pass and just check green.

PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: the epic plan (plans:202608/ci_green_restore.md) lists only 6 sys.modules-patching modules for modguard; tests/test_core_facade/ had 8 more with the identical parent-only pattern — worth correcting the plan text so later readers do not treat the list as exhaustive.

Added tests/_rust_extension_module_helpers.py (patch_rust_extension / install_fake_rust_extension / evict_rust_extension) that moves sase_core_rs.sase_core_rs with its parent via monkeypatch, so teardown restores both together. Routed all 14 patch sites through it: the 6 modules named in the plan plus 8 more in tests/test_core_facade/ with the identical parent-only pattern. Added tests/test_rust_extension_module_helpers.py pinning the helper contract (submodule evicted with parent; re-import while patched rebinds; extension still importable after teardown). Verified against the reported failure with a scratch pytest probe: the old setitem/delitem pattern reproduces 'NameError: name sase_core_rs is not defined' from the installed wheel's __init__.py:3, the new helper does not. just install + just check green (all lint gates + scoped tests, exit 0); 328 tests across tests/test_core_facade + the core/agent-scan modules pass both serially and under -n 4 xdist worker splits.

LAND VERIFICATION (sase-gg.land, 2026-08-06, master 8fcc2520f).

=== STEP 1 — PHASE VERIFICATION (read the source and the commits, not just the notes) ===

sase-gg.1 modguard (08f1b28f8) — CONFIRMED. tests/_rust_extension_module_helpers.py evicts sase_core_rs.sase_core_rs via monkeypatch.delitem BEFORE patching or deleting the parent, so both are restored together at teardown and any re-import behind the patch takes the cache-miss path. Counted the call sites myself: 14 test modules import the helper (the 6 named in the plan plus 8 under tests/test_core_facade/), and a repo-wide grep for setitem/delitem(sys.modules, RUST_EXTENSION_...) finds no surviving raw patch site. tests/test_rust_extension_module_helpers.py pins the helper contract rather than the wheel's robustness, so it stays valid on both the current and hardened wheels. Ran the 14 modules plus the helper tests: 271 passed serially AND 271 passed under -n 4 xdist splits, which is where the defect actually manifested.

sase-gg.2 apptitle (18c681ca8) — CONFIRMED. Both on-mount tests now call _wait_for_mount_state_loads(), a 15s-deadline poll on app._mount_state_loads_done — the barrier _startup_loads.py:150 sets in its finally, matching the existing ace_page.py:168 idiom. The sibling test that previously passed for the wrong reason was fixed too, as the plan required.

sase-gg.3 detailrace (7a5a40b14) — CONFIRMED. The test now intercepts page.app.set_timer to capture the debouncer's callback instead of racing the 150ms window (plan-sanctioned option 2). 'assert calls == []' immediately after the two j presses is what pins the contract: no intermediate row-1 load can occur without a timer firing. DEFAULT_DEBOUNCE_S was left alone, per Out of scope. 23 tests across the two repaired files pass.

sase-gg.4 coreinit — PARTIALLY LANDED, see OPEN ITEM below. sase-org/sase-core PR #89 ships an explicit python/sase_core_rs/__init__.py binding the submodule by name; it is still OPEN.

sase-gg.5 verify — CLOSED WITHOUT EVIDENCE; THE LAND AGENT REDID IT. sase bead history shows sase-gg.5 was closed at 18:46:05Z by bbugyi200.athena.u6 with no note and no reason, not by the phase agent. Its chat transcript ends mid-wait on a backgrounded just check-full and a CI monitor, so the phase's exit criteria were never confirmed on the bead. The transcript does record it completing the adverse-timing controls: negative controls reproduce the original race (slow mount loads for apptitle, a real >150ms inter-keypress gap for detailrace) and the repaired tests survive both. I re-ran the phase's gate myself; results below.

=== STEP 1b — EXIT-CRITERIA GATE (equivalent to just check-full) ===
- just check: all 10 lint gates green (fmt python/markdown, keep-sorted, ruff, mypy, pyscripts, changelog, symvision, toobig), SASE validation green, committed plans green, scoped tests green (34 of 2346 files, contexts baseline present).
- Full just test: 26042 passed, 7 skipped, 0 failed in 145.96s. check-full is exactly those lint gates plus this run, so the phase's required gate is satisfied.
- CI, epic's own commit (run 31120622893, sha 08f1b28f8): NOT a real failure. test (3.12), test (3.14) and coverage-contexts all show conclusion 'cancelled' — superseded by the next push at 17:24Z — and visual-test died in 'Set up job' with 'Service Unavailable' (plan Class 1). test (3.13) passed.
- CI, first COMPLETE post-epic run (run 31123018619, sha baebfcd21): every job that acquired a runner is green — test (3.12), test (3.14), coverage-contexts, lint, perf-floors, build-core, published-core-minimum-smoke. The 3.12 coverage leg and coverage-contexts are precisely the legs the NameError storm and the detail-panel race were killing. The two red jobs (visual-test, test (3.13)) failed with 'The job was not acquired by Runner of type hosted', i.e. Class 1 platform failure, not a regression.
- The newest master run (31125302652, sha 8fcc2520f) is still queued after 47 minutes and its sibling Publish/Deploy Docs workflows on the same sha died to the same runner-acquisition failure. GitHub runner capacity is degraded right now; per the plan this is Class 1 and must not be treated as an epic regression.

=== STEP 2 — INTEGRATION WITH POST-EPIC CHANGES ===
Reviewed every commit landed since the epic's first commit (7a5a40b14) plus a15f409dd, which landed between epic creation and the epic's commits:
- a15f409dd (docs(artifact-ref), sase-fq.8) — comments and a docstring only; no interaction.
- baebfcd21 (fix(sdd-store) agents-sidecar degradation) — touches src/sase/sdd, doctor, and SDD tests. Verified its new and modified tests introduce no sys.modules patching and no TUI pilot synchronization, so nothing to route through the epic's helper. Its own 'pin four tests to tmp_path/chdir' change is an ambient-CWD isolation fix in a different subsystem; same spirit, no overlap or duplication.
- 8fcc2520f (feat(ace-tui) FAMILY MEMBERS roster) — adds ACE TUI tests and a PNG golden. Verified its new async tests already synchronize through real barriers (wait_for_startup, wait_for_visual_idle, page.wait_for) rather than bare pilot.pause(), so they do not reintroduce the apptitle/detailrace pattern.
No post-epic commit duplicates, conflicts with, or needs rewiring to what this epic added. The residual bare pilot.pause() calls in tests/ace/tui/test_custom_gate_modal.py are modal-driven, not mount-loads or debouncer synchronization, and are outside this epic's scope.

=== STEP 3 — FOLLOW-UP TRIAGE (every proposal accounted for) ===
1. sase-gg.1's PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP (the plan named only 6 sys.modules modules; 8 more existed) — DECLINED, no bead. The plan is being marked done, so no future agent executes it, and the discrepancy is already durably recorded in sase-gg.1's note and in commit 08f1b28f8's message. Editing a terminal plan's phase text would rewrite the historical record for no reader benefit.
2. sase-gg.4's PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP (sase-core wheel-smoke never exercises the del-sys.modules re-import path) — FILED as task sase-gh (small, ready) via /sase_new_task. Checked all task statuses and the only in-progress epic (this one): not a duplicate of sase-fs, whose remediation is downstream failure reporting in this repo, and not caused by this epic. Its description records that it must land after PR #89 merges, since the check fails against the current package init by design.
3. sase-fs (pre-existing READY task, the downstream symptom: ~850 then 27 sase_core_rs NameErrors on the 3.12 coverage leg) — NOTED with the root cause and the fix, not closed. This epic answers its 'reproduce or explain' half; its 'fail loudly and once instead of 850 times' half (an import smoke check or session-start guard) is still unbuilt, so I left the close decision to owner triage rather than closing another agent's ready task.
4. sase-ge (pre-existing READY task, GitHub Actions platform failures read as false red) — CORROBORATED with a +1 carrying two fresh occurrences. New information beyond the existing report: the failure mode has widened past ci.yml to the Publish and Deploy Docs workflows and to the sase-core repo, so a fix scoped only to ci.yml would leave false red behind; and it has now cost two consecutive epics their landing signal, including sase-gg.5's abandoned verification. No new bead — same underlying issue.
5. Plan Class 1 (GitHub outage) — no bead, per the plan's explicit 'Action: none. Do not file a bead for this class.' Re-ran the two runner-acquisition-failed CI workflows on sase-core PR #89 (31120460060, 31120460122), which is the plan's prescribed response.

=== OPEN ITEM CARRIED PAST THIS CLOSE ===
sase-core PR #89 is still OPEN. Its first CI attempt lost both jobs to 'The job was not acquired by Runner of type hosted'; I re-ran them and they are queued. The sase-gg.4 agent deliberately did not merge because merging triggers release-plz's automated PyPI publish, and I am upholding that: publishing is outward-facing and irreversible and belongs to the project owner. This does NOT block the epic's stated goal — modguard makes this repo immune regardless of which wheel is installed, which is why CI is green today on the published 0.18.4 wheel that still carries the defect. What remains is stopping the defect at its source for every other consumer. Owner action: merge sase-org/sase-core#89 once its CI is green, then work sase-gh.
